label: L-03
title: The cutover hands V2's and Antimatter's only pause authority to a global Pauser whose `pause()` loop already reverts `EnforcedPause` on two pre-paused registered contracts; Phase 8 asserts registration, not a working breaker
fingerprintProvenance: Copied verbatim from reports/31/script-audits/stable-staker-v2-cutover/classified-findings.json (not recomputed). finding-manager cross-check: sha256(fingerprintBasis) reproduces it byte-for-byte.
description: Phase 7's own NatSpec states the invariant it relies on: "`Pauser.pause()` loops `pause()` over every registered contract with no try/catch, and OZ `_pause` reverts on an already-paused contract, so a paused registered V1 would brick the protocol-wide emergency pause." It therefore unpauses V1, sets `v2.setPauser(PAUSER)` and `antimatter.setPauser(PAUSER)`, and registers both. On mainnet today, two registered contracts are already paused: index 2 `0x3984eBC84d45a889dDAc595d13dc0aC2E54819F4` and index 4 `0xf5F91E8240a0320CAC40b799B25F944a61090E5B`. So the loop reverts before it reaches V1 (index 18), V2 (28) or Antimatter (29). After Phase 7, `StableStakerV2.pause()` is `onlyPauser`, so OWNER cannot pause V2 without first sending `setPauser(OWNER)`. Story Decision 9 flagged the pre-paused contracts for 'human attention', but at 1c1608c the script neither checks nor handles them, and Phase 8's 'pausers registered' assertion passes regardless.
impact: After the cutover, the permissionless EYE-burn emergency stop is non-functional for every registered contract. That includes the new V2, which custodies all migrated principal (~5.75k USD across 29 positions), and Antimatter, whose `annihilate` mints unbacked phUSD. Incident response falls back to the Ledger owner sending 2 transactions per contract. The condition existed before the cutover, but this script extends it to the two new contracts, and its own rationale assumes the breaker works.
attackPath: 1. Pre-existing on mainnet: PhlimboEA V1 0x3984eBC8... (index 2) and old USDC yield strategy 0xf5F91E82... (index 4) are registered with Pauser and already paused (cast call paused()==true, live).
2. The cutover sets V2/Antimatter pauser to Pauser and registers both; Phase 8 asserts isRegistered only.
3. During a future incident, an EYE holder calls Pauser.pause(); the loop reverts EnforcedPause (0xd93c0665) at index 2 before reaching V1 (18), V2 (28) or Antimatter (29).
4. The owner calling V2.pause() directly reverts 'StableStaker: only pauser'; the owner must first send v2.setPauser(OWNER) and then pause(), per contract.

classification.likelihood: low as a standalone issue (it needs a concurrent incident to matter); certain as a latent condition (verified live).
classification.assumptions: A non-malicious owner who believes, as the script's own Phase-7 NatSpec does, that the global breaker is live.
classification.externalRequirements: A separate incident requiring an emergency pause.
remediesEnumerated: Pauser.unregister(x) is onlyOwner and requires x.pauser() != Pauser, so the clean fix is setPauser(away) on each stale contract, then Pauser.unregister: 2 tx per contract, no code change.

Owner can unpause the two stale contracts (unpause is owner-or-pauser on these contracts). This is NOT recommended for retired contracts, because unpausing PhlimboEA V1 or the old USDC strategy may re-open deprecated entry points.
Per-contract fallback during an incident: setPauser(OWNER) + pause() on V2/Antimatter (2 tx each).
Note: Pauser.unpause() also loops with no try/catch, so the global unpause is symmetric-fragile once any member is unpaused.
Conclusion: remediable without code change; not permanent.

severityRationale: A non-obvious owner footgun (Law 3): the script's own comments show the author believes the loop works and deliberately unpauses V1 to keep it working, while two other members already break it. That is surprising to a competent owner, so it is in scope. Not Medium for this entry point: the break predates the script, no exploit is enabled by it, it removes a defence-in-depth control, and the owner retains a working (slower) pause path on every contract with no code change. Flagged for human review because the protocol-wide condition, affecting 30 contracts, is arguably more serious than its slice here.
recommendation: Before (or as part of) the cutover, remediate the registry: either unpause `0x3984eBC8…` and `0xf5F91E82…`, or `setPauser` them away and `Pauser.unregister` them. Add a Phase 0/8 check that iterates `Pauser.getPausableContracts()` and requires `!paused()` for each, or in preview simulates `Pauser.pause()` from an EYE-funded prank inside a `snapshotState/revertToState`, so that 'registered' means 'actually pausable'. Prefer setPauser-away + Pauser.unregister for the two retired contracts over unpausing them. Track the pre-existing registry brick as a separate ledger entry (see outOfSliceNote).
evidence: Fork @25975869 after a full cutover (fork-logs/h-B.log): EYE-funded actor `Pauser.pause()` -> `PAUSER_LOOP|REVERTED|0xd93c0665` (EnforcedPause()); per-contract prank-as-Pauser `pause()`: `PAUSE_ONE|2|0x3984eBC84d45a889dDAc595d13dc0aC2E54819F4|REVERT|0xd93c0665`, `PAUSE_ONE|4|0xf5F91E8240a0320CAC40b799B25F944a61090E5B|REVERT|0xd93c0665`, all other 28 incl. `|18|0xbce8...(V1)|ok`, `|28|0x8482...(V2)|ok`, `|29|0x10EB...(Antimatter)|ok`; `OWNER_PAUSE_V2|REVERT| StableStaker: only pauser`. Live `cast call` confirms `paused()==true, pauser()==Pauser` for both at the fork block. Phase 8 checks only `IPauserRegistry(PAUSER).isRegistered(address(v2))` / `(address(antimatter))`.

outOfSliceNote: The root cause (two pre-paused retired contracts left registered with Pauser) predates and lies outside stable-staker-v2-cutover. It should be tracked as its own entry, not only as a limb of this finding: file a separate phoenix-phase-2-staging ledger finding against the mainnet Pauser registry (an ops or registry-hygiene entry point) and rate it there on its protocol-wide impact. The Pauser repo is not a registered audit project; consider registering it. This finding covers only the script's slice: it extends a dead breaker to two new funds-holding contracts, and Phase 8 certifies registration as if it were pausability.
